title: Erdos607
abstract: Machine-checked upper bound on Erdős problem 607. For n ≥ 2 let F(n) be the number of distinct multiplicity sets A(P) that can arise from a collection P of n points of the plane, where A(P) is the set of block sizes (point counts) of the lines determined by P. The proof shows that the lines of P form a pairwise-balanced design on the n points (every pair of points lies on exactly one line, and each line contains at least two points), so A(P) is exactly the set of block sizes of such a PBD. Hence F(n) is bounded by the number of PBD profile sets on n points, and the Colbourn–Phelps–Rödl (1984) Theorem 2.4 bound exp(c·√n) on that quantity gives F(n) ≤ exp(c·√n) for every n ≥ 2. The bound is stated for n ≥ 2 — the range where the bound is meaningful (a single point determines no line) — so the hypothesis is non-vacuous. The CPR-1984 PBD bound is a published theorem and is taken as the hypothesis hCPR; it is cited, not re-proved here. Together with the Szemerédi–Trotter (1983) lattice-grid lower bound F(n) ≥ exp(c'·√n) (also cited, not re-proved), the order of growth is F(n) = exp(Θ(√n)). This repository contains zero axioms and zero sorry in the proof development (the only sorry is the deliberate statement surface in Challenge.lean).
